teaching: Every station (maqam) — whether of a prophet, a wasi, or an Imam — is connected by the maddah (substance) that flows from the First Intellect.
The maddah is always issued continuously from the First Intellect and never ceases.
The First Intellect is named 'al-Hayy al-Qayyum' (the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining) in the Quran; this is its attribute.
The Greatest Name of Allah (Ism al-A'zam) is present within 'al-Hayy al-Qayyum', as it is within 'Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram'.
The tasbih (glorification) assigned to Sunday is 'al-Hayy al-Qayyum'.
The Dua al-Hayat is said to contain the Ism al-A'zam (though not pinpointed); it was revealed separately from Allah, not in the manner of the Quran.
The Dua al-Hayat is a du'a of Maulana 'Ali, who valued it so highly that he kept it in his turban.

The Ism al-A'zam refers to the First Intellect, not to the mubda' ta'ala (Transcendent Originator), who is beyond all names, indications, and qualities; all dealings occur through the First Intellect.

'al-Hayy al-Qayyum' means the First Intellect both lives by the maddah received from the mubda' ta'ala and gives life by passing it to lower intellects according to their capacity to receive (istiqhaq), never giving all of what it receives.
The intellects after the First Intellect differ in precedence (sabaqiyat) and acuity of vision (hiddat-e-nazar), but their understanding is the same.
The Originator created every intellect with the same first-level endowment of three powers — knowledge, life, and power; how each subsequently used them determined its rank.
The chain of maddah and ta'yid flows continuously from the First Intellect and is not cut off even for the blink of an eye (la yanqati'u turfata 'ayn).

When a prophet, wasi, or Imam manifests power, miracles, and actions that bewilder the intellects of creatures, that action is attributed to the higher one who looks upon him — the muhtajib (veiled one) and mumiddu (aider).
When a prophet, wasi, or Imam manifests weakness, pain, illness, or human states, that is attributed to the ghilaf (covering) / hijab / nasut (human form), not to the essential self.
The nasut is extracted from the world of nature (alam al-tabi'ah), formed from the airy souls (nufus rihiyyah), and obtained through physical birth (wiladat jismaniyyah).
Ghulu (raising an Imam above his station) and qulu/qassar (diminishing him below his station) are both impermissible.
When some elevated Maulana 'Ali to divinity, he warned them, and when they refused to listen he ordered them burned; later du'at like Mughira did the same regarding Ja'far al-Sadiq.
One must not believe that any prophet, wasi, or Imam is an originating god (ilah mubdi') or lord; they merely nurture lower ranks with the wisdom (hikmah) by which they are aided from above.

All stations and hudud negate divinity and lordship from themselves, affirming that the power to originate from nothing belongs only to the mubda' ta'ala, Originator of all (Mubdi' al-kull) and their Creator.
Quran: 'And whoever of them says, I am a god besides Him — that one We recompense with Hell; thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.'
Nimrod's punishment is more severe than Yazid's because Nimrod claimed divinity for himself while Yazid did not.
The word jaza' (recompense) carries two senses — punishment and reward.

Many people, seeing the dazzling miracles and astounding deeds manifested at 'Ali's hands, committed ghulu and claimed he was a god who creates and provides, neither born nor begetting and without equal — which Allah cursed as misguidance (dalal) and disbelief (kufr).

The correct obligatory belief is that the Prophet Muhammad is the most excellent of the intellects of the world of nature (afdalu 'uqul al-'alam al-tabi'ah) and the noblest of the world of the hudud of religion.
The 'intellects of the world of nature' are those presently in potentiality (bil-quwwah) — the veils — who will one day become actual intellects.
The miracles 'Ali manifested were from the support (ta'yid) of the First Intellect, and reached him only through the mediation of the Prophet.
The Prophet remains the mediator (wasita) for everything always, even after his passing.

Jibra'il conveyed his salam to 'Ali and declared the Prophet 'sayyid al-anbiya wal-mursalin wa khatam al-nabiyyin' and 'Ali 'Amir al-Mu'minin'; thus the title Amir al-Mu'minin came to 'Ali from Allah through Jibra'il.
Every Imam of the time is Amir al-Mu'minin, but when 'Amir al-Mu'minin' is said without a name it denotes 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.
The Prophet is 'Ali's hadd, teacher, nurturer, and the one who raised him to his rank; he made 'Ali his successor (caliph) in his community, and 'Ali is his hujjat in his lifetime.
The Prophet's rank in the physical world corresponds to the First Intellect (al-'aql al-awwal al-sabiq), and 'Ali's rank in religion corresponds to the first emanation (munba'ath al-awwal).
The Prophet is like the male (dhakar) and the sky (sama'); 'Ali is like the female who accepts from him (untha qabilah) and the earth (ard) that absorbs the pure water descending from the sky.
Quran 'wa ta'iyaha udhunun wa'iyah' (that a retaining ear might retain it) refers to 'Ali, who said 'that ear is me' (tilka al-udhun ana) and is called 'udhun khayr' (an ear of goodness).

After the Prophet's death 'Umar regretted unasked questions; 'Ali answered them — e.g. that dreams during the sensory soul's ascent through the heavens are true and those on its return are false — having remembered what 'Umar had forgotten.

Nothing is received directly from the First Intellect; in the present life the Prophet is the last and closest intermediary, while 'Ali's sermon 'ana al-awwal, ana al-akhir' relates to the 'ayn level.
'Ali said the Messenger taught him a thousand chapters from his treasured hidden knowledge, and from each chapter a thousand more opened ('allamani Rasulullah min makhnun 'ilmihi alfa bab).

At 'Ali's birth (from Fatima bint Asad in the Kaaba) he fixed his first gaze on the Prophet, who said 'khassastani bin-nazr wa khassastuka bil-'ilm' and 'Ana madinat al-'ilm wa 'Ali babuha', though his mother had named him Haidar.
key_terms: Ana madinat al-ilm wa Ali babuha

teaching: When the Prophet passed, 'Ali stood in the world of religion at the station of the First Intellect, and his hujjat (Bibi Fatima Zahra) at the station of the first emanation (munba'ath al-awwal).
Fatima Zahra is the successor (khalifa) of the Prophet — her footsteps fall where his fall — and the greatest hujjat of her husband: 'hujjatu ba'liha wa khalifatu abiha'.

It is obligatory to believe that the Prophet and 'Ali are in a single station and single rank (manzilah wahidah, martabah wahidah) with no superiority of one over the other, differing only in precedence (sabaqiyat).
The Prophet illustrated his equality with 'Ali by joining the index and middle fingers ('ana wa anta ya 'Ali ka-hatayn'), where one finger precedes — indicating Abu Talib always preceded the Prophet.
key_terms: ana wa anta ya Ali ka-hatayn

teaching: Whoever raises one of the Prophet/'Ali pair and lowers the other commits ghulu and falls short (qassara); the curse of Allah is upon anyone who holds the contrary belief.
Having explained the reality of the beginning (ibtida') and the praiseworthy return of the believers, the text turns to the unpraiseworthy return — 'wa hadha haqiqatu al-ibtida' wa al-ma'ad'.
The author has unveiled these matters explicitly and plainly without symbol or indication; such speech is unveiled only by the great Du'at, who are 'our hudud', and a prayer is made for their reward.
Knowing the return of the opponents completes the believer's form and elevates his rank (li-taktamila suratuka), just as 'la ilaha illa Allah' requires knowing both its negation and affirmation.
Knowledge is of two kinds — knowing the awliya Allah and knowing the opponents who are other than them — and both are necessary.

One should strive in good deeds to join the noble company in the sacred enclosure (hadhirat al-quds) — Bab al-Abwab, where the forms of the twelve islands gather — in the vicinity of Rabb al-'alamin, who is the Imam of the Time.
The opponent of truth, through his hostility, acquires the deeds of the people of evil, which form a dark form (suratun zulmaniyyah) — the inverse of the believer's luminous form.
At death the opponent's dark form (his vile concept) is stripped away, terrifying and alienating him — this is the first of its punishments.
The dark form's origin is the darkness that fell upon him at the time of his sin in the world of beginning (alam al-ibtida'), when he did not heed the 'ashir and did not repent.

This darkness, the head and tail (ra's wa dhanab, i.e. Rahu and Ketu), acts as a magnet for the dark satanic forms because of the affinity (munasabah) between them — 'as the person is, so are his angels'.
Ra's wa dhanab (Rahu and Ketu) lie below the sphere of the moon; they are not a planetary sphere but conceptual, non-visible places that nonetheless exist, serving as a center for the vile forms.
The vile forms residing there produce the harmful sorrows of the world, troubling and perplexing the believers.

Those in the lowest ranks can ascend gradually from being musirr (insistent on sin), for qudrat wills that the insistent and wretched enter faith; this occurs across the cycles (adwar) and eras (aqwar).

Those who ascend are entrusted with very great services spanning entire cycles (adwar), gaining great luminosity and transparency, so that on their return in human form they reach very high stations; some current du'at were formerly musirrin and mustakbirin (arrogant).
There are three punishments: the lowest ('adhab al-adna), the middle ('adhab al-awsat), and the greatest ('adhab al-akbar).

The lowest punishment ('adhab al-adna) occurs in the physical world, descending through human (Zanj/Habshi), then bear and monkey, wild animals, birds, down to the mineral level, ending in tar where no da'wah is presented.

At each change of form the da'wah of the Imam of the Time is presented; acceptance (which is rare) leads to ascent and refusal to descent, until the tar punishment where no argument or da'wah is offered — a mercy of qudrat that ends there.

Volcanic lava represents souls being returned toward human form, released from the punishment of rock; the land becoming fertile signifies their ascent, and the minerals (namaz) that form, when eaten, carry them upward.

Lunar and solar eclipses are caused by the vile forms gaining mastery over and awareness of the Imam's hidden plans, whereupon their mischief against believers increases; hence one should be engaged in prayer and supplication during an eclipse.

At the death of the Prophet's son Ibrahim a solar eclipse occurred; the Prophet rejected the people's claim that it was connected to his son's death, declaring the eclipse a sign of Allah with no connection to it.

When the Prophet wished to enter Ibrahim's grave, Mawla al-Ka'inat ('Ali) descended instead; and Ibrahim was made a ransom for Imam Husayn, Jibril having offered the Prophet a choice of which to be tried.

The Prophet wept over his four-year-old son Ibrahim (son of Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah); challenged by the hypocrites, he declared his natural grief — without mourning rites or tearing clothes — permissible.
Hypocrites (munafiqun) arose only in Madinah; in Makkah there were only disbelievers and polytheists or Muslims.

A gathering of the young children of past prophets who died young assembled at Ibrahim's death and later passed to Bibi Fatima, who is therefore called 'khulasatu al-jawhar al-islami' (the essence of the Islamic jewel).
Those who died before the wilayah of 'Ali was proclaimed also passed to Bibi Fatima's gathering, in which the highest form is that of Mawlana Hamzah.

Among the opponents, those of few sins who answered a prophet's call, submitted, and served are ground (sahik) and then ascend through the praiseworthy isthmus (barzakh al-su'ud) in minerals, plants, and animals until they obtain human form, then respond and ascend.

Ascent occurs only by accepting the noble da'wah / the call of the Imam of the Time; prayer, Hajj, and zakat alone are of no avail (though they bring one nearer), and consciously accepting the noble da'wah is the noblest deed.
Children who died young — such as Ibrahim and Asghar bin Husayn — hold very high ranks, the ranks of great du'at, despite having had no consciousness of the da'wah.

In the opponent's return, his vile conception departs before his body; his body is buried after his soul has spread within it — a degradation, since it is reprehensible for the high soul to spread in the body.
Cremation produces the same state as burial but with greater punishment, because the cremated have hastened and inflicted upon themselves the punishment of fire.

From the opponent (disbeliever, polytheist, enemy) and from all animals only the airy soul (nafs hawaiyyah) — the vapor he inhaled — departs at death, whereas from the believer the spiritual souls (nufus rihiyyah) depart.

When the opponent's body is buried it rots and stinks and writhes in the dust, and each of the four humors returns to its element-mother: yellow bile to fire, blood to air, phlegm to water, black bile to dust — gradually; this is the first of his punishments.
All of this is preserved by the power of the Planner (qudrat al-mudabbir); the ascending parts gather as rain in another form, dissolve into the dust, and become plants that are eaten.

The impure forms shelter in wildernesses, wastelands, filthy places, sewers, streams, and ravines, appear in people's dreams, and incite acts of lewdness in enmity to the people of truth; they are the blameworthy jinn, the devils (shayatin), and rebellious 'afarit harmful to mankind.
The believer's first reward is that his luminous form appears with radiance upon his body at the time of his death.

Sayyidna Muhammad Burhanuddin in Al-Anwar al-Latifah explains that when a believer dies a comforting light appears, which is the gathered happiness he brought to his believing brethren in life, given the form of light.

The dark form departs from the deceased opponent's soul and roams the horizon seeking to ascend (impossible) and to re-enter the body for its bodily pleasures (impossible), then roams the air — what the common people call munaf — with a forty-day respite.
The term munaf denotes the screaming and wailing born of dread (wahshat), and is not the plural of munif (from anf, meaning high-nosed / honorable).

The vile conceptions descend (hulul) into an ignorant impure woman, a dirty boy, or the like, possess them, speak through their tongues, whisper, and command sin; sometimes they leave and sometimes they cling until death.

Possession requires a pre-existing inclination in the host, for 'al-khabithuna lil-khabithat wal-khabithat lil-khabithin' (evil is for evil); without inclination nothing can occur, and even the awliya Allah are not wholly free of such inclinations.

Children who do not purify after the washroom spread impurity, and devils lick the hands of children who sleep with food on them, causing their night crying; therefore children's hands and feet should be washed before sleep.
The du'a 'Allahumma khalaqtani' states that the devil runs unseen in our blood, whispering and urging evil; qudrat nonetheless preserves us through our prayers, good deeds, and intentions.
The Prophet's prayers are short and easy to memorize, and through them he conferred great graces and protections upon the ummah.

Jibril taught the Prophet the prayer 'Allahumma inni as'aluka al-'afw wa al-'afiyah wa al-mu'afah fi al-dunya wa al-akhirah, ya arham al-rahimin' for times of worry or sickness, which the Prophet reserved for the Muslim ummah rather than himself.

Sayyidna 'Ali bin Sulayman compiled short prayers taught by Sayyidna Muhammad bin Fahd, including the tasbih 'Amanun min Allah wa Rasulihi, ya sayyidi, ya karim', on whose realities nearly forty pages were written.

After a bad death the impure forms endure seven plunges of punishment (al-nahas), the first being cast in the form of a Zanj (Abyssinian human form); when such a one is eaten by a male and female, an evil offspring resembling his parents appears.
The opponent's soul spreads in his body (a regression), becomes dense with sins, then dies and dissolves to become a plant, and passes through forms of monkeys, langurs, and bears.
Incantations (ruqa), amulets (aza'im), and the recitation of the Quran drive these forms away in cases of seizure/epilepsy (sar'); they flee and turn away.

The forms shelter in dreadful filthy places, bathhouses, and places where wine is drunk, then ascend to the tail (dhanab) — the two knots (ughdatayn), a darkness called dhanab and ra's outside the celestial sphere — and are nourished as monkeys, dogs, and pigs and all blameworthy forms.

The forms become a killing-poison plant (bitter and destructive), descend lower, then enter the most blameworthy minerals — glass (zaj), sulfur (kibrit), iron (hadid), lead (usas), and brass — before passing into animals.

The opponent's return is by transformation (istihalah) and birth (wiladah), NOT by the soul transferring from a dead body into another; the doctrine of transmigration (tanasukh) is misguidance and ignorance whose believer is destroyed and cursed.

When the lesser punishment (seven stages) is completed near the rising of the Qa'im, the opponent is joined with fire, becomes a plant eaten by his kind, a human person is born, is gathered at the rising of the Qa'im, rebuked for his past deeds, slaughtered, burned by fire descending from the ether, and led to Sijjin (the rock, Sakhar) to abide in the greatest punishment.

The Great Cycle of the greatest punishment lasts 360,000 years (stated as three hundred thousand plus one hundred thousand plus sixty and one thousand), and is reckoned as 360,000 multiplied by 360,000.
There is no remorse during the greatest punishment; remorse exists only in the lesser punishment, at every cycle (karr) and plunge (ghark), for at the greatest the pen has dried (jaffa al-qalam).
The greatest punishment (Sakhar, one Great Cycle) is only for the great opposites (azdad al-kibar) who opposed and killed the awliya Allah, and for the essence of sins, the wicked, and the evil.
The general rabble (kafat al-hamaj al-ri'a' — ignorant followers of evil) do not reach the greatest punishment, by Allah's care, because every servant is recompensed only by the measure of his deed.

From the deceased rabble only the airy soul departs; he dissolves through the isthmuses to the lesser punishment per his deeds, returns by transformation and birth to human form, and is presented the da'wah — purified if he responds, returned to deserved punishment a second time if he refuses — because Allah is Just, does not oppress, and does not break His promise.
The entire purpose of the genesis of creation is its purification and salvation from sin; whoever is purified ascends, while whoever refuses and shows enmity to the hudud is inverted and falls.
The believer is exhorted to be eager for action, purification, and the lightening of sins, and not to be deceived by the transient world.
'Ali said 'takhaffafu talhaqu' (lighten yourselves and you will catch up), for 'the first of you await the arrival of the last of you' (fa-innama yantaziru bi-awwalikum qudum akhirikum).
This teaching is the secret of the celestial realm (sirr al-malakut), entrusted as a trust (amanah) to be protected and concealed from everyone except those named.

Some who ascend reach the rank of bab al-abwab after thousands of years of service; du'at, ma'adhib, and hudud al-da'wah who serve sincerely are recompensed with high ranks in their future cycles (karrat).

The mothers of the Imams (ummahat al-a'immah) are infallible (ma'sumah), batul (without menstrual blood), and pure; they attain this honor because 'service has preceded them' (qad sabaqathunna al-khidam) in the times of the Imams, as with Muhammad bin al-Walid or Muhammad bin Fawad.

In the next cycle (wahdah) the template is the same but succession (khilafat) is established; the higher veil ascends and becomes the muhtajib — so high it becomes a veil for other veils — and the purified excesses (fuzalat) ascend to become their veils (hijabat).

Salman al-Farsi was born a Parsi non-Muslim in Fars, hidden since childhood, came in search of truth, and reached Madinah around 2 Hijri (absent throughout the Makkan period); brought as a slave, the Prophet freed him via 300 date palms planted by him and 300 by the Muslims plus gold.
Salman recognized the Prophet by three signs: that he accepts a gift but does not eat charity, and that the seal of prophethood was on his back.
Because of Salman's great spiritual progress, 'Salman minna Ahl al-Bayt' (Salman is from us, the Ahl al-Bayt) was declared.

The Ahl al-Bayt do not eat zakat because zakat is filth (mayl) and they are pure; and in Quran 'khudh min amwalihim sadaqatan...', 'salli 'alayhim' means 'pray for them' (a source of tranquility), not 'send salutations upon them'.

A non-Ahl-al-Bayt person may eat the meat of a sadaqah or vow (nadhr) goat; for an 'aqiqah its bones must not be broken and the breastfeeding mother of the child must not eat it (it reaches the impermissible child via her milk); and one may not eat the meat of an obligatory Hajj sacrifice but may eat that of a voluntary one.

It is a rare exceptional (istisna') case that a man becomes a woman or a woman becomes a man across cycles (karrat); this is no degradation but a high rank, as Sayyidna Sulayman bin Hasan is said to become Mawlatuna Zaynab in later cycles.
